rules.description: Freeze placeholder comments and scaffold leftovers.
rules.what: Catch placeholder comments, boilerplate words, and scaffold leftovers before they become repository debt.
rules.why: These patterns usually indicate unfinished work or copied scaffolding, which makes reviews and future edits harder to trust.

rules.description: Freeze marker-heavy comments that accumulate as slop debt.
rules.what: Catch repeated TODO/FIXME/XXX markers that turn into noise instead of actionable work.
rules.why: Marker spam makes the codebase harder to review because unresolved notes compete with real implementation detail.

rules.what: Reject files that contain no implementation or meaningful content.
rules.why: Empty files are often failed edits or placeholders that should either be filled or deleted.

rules.description: Freeze overly long lines that hurt readability.
rules.what: Keep implementation readable by rejecting lines that have become too dense to review comfortably.
rules.why: Long lines hide multiple concerns in one statement and make diff review much noisier.

rules.description: Freeze UI buttons that do not declare an explicit action hook.
rules.what: Require every button to expose a clear action so its effect is discoverable and reviewable.
rules.why: Buttons without explicit actions create dead-end UI that looks interactive but cannot be traced reliably.

rules.description: Freeze button types so UI intent is explicit.
rules.what: Require button elements to declare an explicit type so forms and interactions remain predictable.
rules.why: Implicit button types create subtle form submission and reset behavior that is easy to miss in generated UI.

rules.description: Freeze form labels so the interface remains accessible.
rules.what: Require form controls to expose a clear label or accessible name.
rules.why: Labels make forms usable for assistive technology and reduce the chance that generated UI silently becomes confusing.

rules.description: Freeze the bridge between UI markup and client-side handlers.
rules.what: Require declared UI actions to be wired into the client-side handler graph so the interface is understandable.
rules.why: Action declarations without corresponding handlers create synthetic dead-ends that look complete but collapse under review.

rules.description: Freeze oversized files that are hard to review and maintain.
rules.what: Reject files that exceed the configured size threshold so the codebase stays reviewable.
rules.why: Oversized files often hide monolithic logic or generated content that should be split into smaller, focused units.

rules.description: Freeze rule definitions that do not carry the metadata needed to review and trace them.
rules.what: Require every rule to expose a human-readable description, a clear what/why explanation, and at least one source reference.
rules.why: A policy that cannot be explained, navigated, or traced is not really enforceable; it becomes invisible slop that is hard to debug and easy to bypass.

rules.description: Freeze source references that cannot be read by the dashboard or other tooling.
rules.what: Require every source reference attached to a rule to resolve to a real file that can be opened as UTF-8 text.
rules.why: If the policy points at a file the UI cannot inspect, the rule becomes opaque and the repository loses its traceability moat.

rules.description: Freeze hard-coded environment-specific paths and loopback endpoints that make the framework brittle.
rules.what: Require configuration and code to use runtime-derived values instead of absolute machine-specific paths or local-only hosts.
rules.why: Hard-coded paths and loopback endpoints break portability and make the framework behave like a one-machine patchwork instead of a reusable system.
